parameters.content:
## onchain-retention — retention cleanup (task 014-41, deployment.md §10.6)

**Daily.** Three jobs, each deleting or nulling data past its window, each writing ONE row to
`onchain.retention_runs` in the same pass — including a pass that deleted nothing
(`rows_affected = 0`, `outcome = 'ok'`). "Nothing to delete" and "the job did not run" are different
facts and only the written row tells them apart.

| job | target | action | default window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `diagnostics.purge` | `onchain.diagnostics` | delete rows past the window | 90d (floor 90, max = NORMALIZED) |
| `request_trace.raw_null` | `onchain.request_trace` | set `tried_json` to NULL past the window | 90d (floor 90, max = NORMALIZED) |
| `request_trace.purge` | `onchain.request_trace` | delete rows past the window | 365d (floor 365, max 730) |

**The three windows live in `Set Parameters` and nowhere else.** Changing one edits that node; no
query node is touched. The BOUNDS live in `Plan jobs`, because a setting that carried its own maximum
could widen itself.

**A window out of range is REFUSED, not clamped.** The job deletes nothing, its row is written with
`outcome = 'failed'` and the rejected setting named in `detail_json`, and `Check outcomes` throws so
the refusal reaches Telegram through `onchain-error-alert`. A clamped window would delete rows the
operator asked to keep and record the clamped period as the requested one.

**Credential: `Onchain engine state`, NOT `Supabase DB`.** The snapshotter's role has no privilege on
the twelve engine tables (§10.5). Reading `onchain.snapshots` with this credential must be refused by
Postgres — that is the check, not a convention.

**Every write binds base64 as one `$1` parameter.** `queryReplacement` is positional CSV: a comma
breaks it and an empty value silently shifts every later `$N`. Nothing is interpolated into SQL.

`retention_runs` is never itself cleaned: the job that cleaned it would write to it (§4.5.9).

WITH plan AS (SELECT convert_from(decode($1,'base64'),'utf8')::jsonb AS p),
     touched AS (
       DELETE FROM onchain.diagnostics
        WHERE (SELECT (p->>'valid')::boolean FROM plan) IS TRUE
          AND ts < (SELECT (p->>'cutoff')::bigint FROM plan)
       RETURNING 1
     )
SELECT count(*)::bigint AS rows_affected FROM touched;

INSERT INTO onchain.retention_runs
  (id, job, target_table, period_from, period_to, rows_affected, started_at, finished_at, outcome, detail_json)
SELECT id, job, target_table, period_from, period_to, rows_affected, started_at, finished_at, outcome, detail_json
FROM jsonb_to_recordset(convert_from(decode($1,'base64'),'utf8')::jsonb)
  AS x(id text, job text, target_table text, period_from bigint, period_to bigint,
       rows_affected bigint, started_at bigint, finished_at bigint, outcome text, detail_json text)
ON CONFLICT (job, period_from, period_to, started_at) DO NOTHING;

WITH plan AS (SELECT convert_from(decode($1,'base64'),'utf8')::jsonb AS p),
     touched AS (
       UPDATE onchain.request_trace SET tried_json = NULL
        WHERE (SELECT (p->>'valid')::boolean FROM plan) IS TRUE
          AND received_at < (SELECT (p->>'cutoff')::bigint FROM plan)
          AND tried_json IS NOT NULL
       RETURNING 1
     )
SELECT count(*)::bigint AS rows_affected FROM touched;

INSERT INTO onchain.retention_runs
  (id, job, target_table, period_from, period_to, rows_affected, started_at, finished_at, outcome, detail_json)
SELECT id, job, target_table, period_from, period_to, rows_affected, started_at, finished_at, outcome, detail_json
FROM jsonb_to_recordset(convert_from(decode($1,'base64'),'utf8')::jsonb)
  AS x(id text, job text, target_table text, period_from bigint, period_to bigint,
       rows_affected bigint, started_at bigint, finished_at bigint, outcome text, detail_json text)
ON CONFLICT (job, period_from, period_to, started_at) DO NOTHING;

WITH plan AS (SELECT convert_from(decode($1,'base64'),'utf8')::jsonb AS p),
     touched AS (
       DELETE FROM onchain.request_trace
        WHERE (SELECT (p->>'valid')::boolean FROM plan) IS TRUE
          AND received_at < (SELECT (p->>'cutoff')::bigint FROM plan)
       RETURNING 1
     )
SELECT count(*)::bigint AS rows_affected FROM touched;

INSERT INTO onchain.retention_runs
  (id, job, target_table, period_from, period_to, rows_affected, started_at, finished_at, outcome, detail_json)
SELECT id, job, target_table, period_from, period_to, rows_affected, started_at, finished_at, outcome, detail_json
FROM jsonb_to_recordset(convert_from(decode($1,'base64'),'utf8')::jsonb)
  AS x(id text, job text, target_table text, period_from bigint, period_to bigint,
       rows_affected bigint, started_at bigint, finished_at bigint, outcome text, detail_json text)
ON CONFLICT (job, period_from, period_to, started_at) DO NOTHING;

INSERT INTO onchain.diagnostics
  (id, ts, severity, event, principal_id, session_id, provider, capability, trace_id, detail_json, created_at)
SELECT id, ts, severity, event, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, detail_json, created_at
FROM jsonb_to_recordset(convert_from(decode($1,'base64'),'utf8')::jsonb)
  AS x(id text, ts bigint, severity text, event text, detail_json text, created_at bigint);
